answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must keep a dedicated process continuously solving short random challenge puzzles; rewards vest only at dawn after a full cycle. An idle or recycled identity restarts its clock, so operators must pay real compute and wall-clock attention per identity. The ember of accrued credit dies on restart. Honest agents spread work across a ridge of machines; a sybil farm must sustain that cost for every fake identity simultaneously, and the ledger caps parallel identities by measured sustained throughput.
